svg.title: Destiny Disrupted: dynasties and the Sunni-Shi'i map, 622-2026
svg.desc: A three-panel infographic. The top panel shows Muslim dynasties inside five broad social periods. The middle panel is a heatmap of Sunni and Shi'i prevalence by region and era. The bottom panel lists nine turning points.

g.text: A visual companion to Tamim Ansary's history of the Islamic world
I. The shape of Muslim society
Political dynasties (bars) inside five broad social periods (band). Green = Sunni dynasty; blue = Shi'i dynasty.
Dominant sect by region and era. Colour reflects broad popular adherence, not the sect of the ruler; dots mark significant minorities or sub-regional majorities.
• Sunni Islam is the majority almost everywhere; Shi'i majorities are concentrated in Iran, Iraq, Azerbaijan and Bahrain,
with large minorities in Lebanon, Yemen, Pakistan and India.
• The decisive shift is Iran after 1501, when the Safavids imposed Twelver Shi'ism; the Ottoman–Safavid frontier then hardened the divide.
• Dynastic patronage changed the political map faster than popular adherence: Buyid and Fatimid power rose and fell, but the demographic map moved slowly.
Simplified: Alevis, Ibadis and other heterodox communities do not fit the Sunni–Shi'i binary and are not shown separately.
